Introduction to Climate Change

Climate change refers to long-term shifts in global temperatures and weather patterns. While climate change is a natural phenomenon, scientific evidence shows that human activities have been the dominant cause of warming since the mid-20th century.

Impact on Ecosystems

The effects of climate change include rising sea levels, melting ice caps, and extreme weather events. These changes threaten biodiversity and disrupt ecosystems worldwide. Scientists have documented widespread impacts on wildlife populations and habitat loss.

Mitigation Strategies

Addressing climate change requires global cooperation and immediate action. Key strategies include transitioning to renewable energy sources, improving energy efficiency, and implementing sustainable land-use practices. Governments, businesses, and individuals all have important roles to play in climate change mitigation.

Future Projections

Climate models project continued warming throughout the 21st century if greenhouse gas emissions remain high. However, limiting global temperature rise to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels is still possible with rapid and far-reaching transitions in energy, land, urban infrastructure, and industrial systems.

Key Statistics

  • Global temperature has risen by approximately 1.1°C since pre-industrial times
  • Arctic sea ice extent has declined by about 13% per decade
  • Sea levels have risen by approximately 20cm in the past century
  • CO2 concentrations have increased by over 40% since the industrial revolution
